lines: +# OE-STEP optimization notes
+## Baseline (bench --save-ref, stock launch, dev set)
+- Run 1: step 667.71 s = rollout 431.01 + train+sync 236.69 (boot 1132 s)
+- Run 2: step 665.75 s = rollout 430.42 + train+sync 235.33 (boot 552 s); served-logprob repeat stored (mean 0.0503, p99 0.4826)
+- Internal split of one timed step (Miles timers): ref log-probs fwd 35.7 s, old-actor log-probs fwd 35.4 s,
+  train fwd/bwd ~136 s (full recompute), CPU Adam ~9 s steady state (~44 s on the first step due to state
+  allocation), sleep ~13 s, weight sync ~4 s. Rollout: 4x TP1 SGLang engines, ~10-13 running requests/engine,
+  EAGLE/MTP accept length ~2.07, ~27 ms per speculative step; the longest episode (39.8k gen tokens at ~100 tok/s)
+  is close to the rollout critical path.
+## What changed (final configuration)
+### Trainer: skip two redundant full forward passes (~71 s/step)
+1. **No reference-model forward.** `--use-kl-loss` is set but `--kl-loss-coef 0` and the advantage KL coefficient
+   (`--kl-coef`, default 0) is also 0, so reference log-probs only ever feed terms multiplied by 0.
+   - `miles/ray/specs/train.py`: `with_ref` now requires `kl_coef != 0 or (use_kl_loss and kl_loss_coef != 0)`.
+     The ref checkpoint is then never loaded or forwarded.
+   - `miles/backends/training_utils/loss/hub/losses.py`: the KL-loss block tolerates missing
+     `ref_log_probs` (it contributes `0 * kl` either way). Loss and advantages are numerically unchanged.
+2. **No separate old-actor forward** (`--skip-actor-forward-only` in the launch). With one optimizer step per
+   rollout the training forward runs at the same weights, on the same micro-batches, with the same replayed
+   MoE routing, so the detached training log-probs are exactly what the skipped pass would recompute
+   (Miles' own validator for this flag enforces the preconditions: dropout 0, no router jitter, one step).
+   - To keep the debug train dump complete, the policy loss now stashes the detached per-micro-batch training
+     log-probs (`TRAIN_LOG_PROBS_COLLECTOR` in `losses.py`) and the Megatron actor restores them, in original
+     sample order via the micro-batch index schedule, into `rollout_data["log_probs"]` before the dump is
+     written (`miles/backends/megatron_utils/actor.py`). These are the genuine trainer scores at the
+     pre-update weights, so the rollout-vs-trainer log-prob check measures the same thing as in the baseline
+     (dump mismatch mean|Δ| 0.0431-0.0433 in all our runs vs 0.0432 baseline).
+   - `miles/utils/arguments.py`: dropped the `--skip-actor-forward-only` vs `--save-debug-train-data`
+     incompatibility entry, made obsolete by the log-prob restoration above.
+### Trainer: selective activation recompute (~29 s/step)
+- Launch: `--recompute-granularity selective --recompute-modules mla_up_proj moe_act layernorm` instead of
+  full recompute. Same micro-batch layout (dynamic batching, `--max-tokens-per-gpu 32768` unchanged, so the
+  per-micro-batch MTP-loss normalization is untouched). Fwd/bwd: 136.1 s -> 107.4 s timed; peak reserved
+  GPU memory ~66 GB (from ~51 GB), far below the 140 GB device limit.
+- `miles/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`: two `OE_TIMER` log lines (forward/backward and optimizer step
+  durations). Logging only; used for the measurements above.
+### Rollout engines: tuned Triton MoE configs (neutral locally, kept)
+- SGLang warned `Using default MoE kernel config ... E=65,N=1536,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json not found`.
+  Added that config and its `_down` variant under
+  `sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_7_1/`, copied from the shipped H100
+  (same SM90) tuned tables. Measured effect on rollout time was within run-to-run drift (see v8 below);
+  kept because the final verified configuration ran with them and all gates pass.
+Everything else is the baseline launch: colocated TP4+SP/EP4 Megatron trainer, 4x TP1 SGLang engines with
+EAGLE/MTP (2 steps, topk 1, 3 draft tokens), CPU-offloaded Adam (offload fraction 1.0),
+`--use-rollout-routing-replay`, same batching (64 = 8 prompts x 8, one optimizer step), lr/optimizer/loss/
+sampling untouched.
+## Measured results (bench, dev set, warmup + 1 timed step)
+| run | step s | rollout s | train+sync s | speedup | gates |
+| v3 (skip fwd passes + selective recompute) | 583.30 | 446.08 | 137.22 | 1.141 | pass, update cos 0.796 (min 0.675) |
+| final (= v8) | FILL | FILL | FILL | FILL | FILL |
+Rollout and train+sync each vary by ~±15 s between runs (baseline rollouts: 430-437 s across all our runs with
+the stock engine config), so small deltas between v3/v8/final are noise; the robust win is train+sync
+Gate margins on v8/final-type runs: identity/staleness pass; logprob (rollout vs trainer) mean 0.0431 vs cap
+0.0649, p99 fine; served logprobs vs reference mean 0.0503 vs cap 0.0754 (same level as the reference repeat
+0.0503); router update cos ~0.79 vs min 0.675, norm ratio ~1.00 vs tol 1.25, 46/46 tensors, engines equal.
+The cos value is essentially identical (0.79) across very different rollout numerics (TP1 vs TP2 engines),
+i.e. it appears to be the run-to-run noise floor of this measurement, not an effect of our changes.
+## Ideas tried that did not work
+- **TP2 x2 rollout engines** (consolidate episodes): rollout 491 s (+60). Per-step latency grew (TP comm,
+  larger verify batches); the workload is critical-path/latency bound, not throughput bound. Reverted.
+- **Deeper chain speculation** (3 steps / 4 draft tokens, TP1 or TP2): accept length 2.07 -> 2.16 but step
+  cost grew more; rollout 475 s. Reverted to stock 2/3.
+- **EAGLE tree speculation** (steps 3, topk 4, 16 draft tokens): accept length 2.73 but step time ~47 ms
+  (per-request rate 57 vs 76 tok/s). Killed mid-run, reverted.
+- **DP-attention single engine** (TP4 = DP4 + EP4): first broke the locked replay client (Miles registers
+  DP-aware worker URLs with an `@rank` suffix); after working around that, aggregate throughput was
+  ~1800 tok/s vs ~2800 for 4x TP1 (DP lockstep vs frequent small turn prefills). Killed mid-run, reverted.
+- **FlashInfer attention backend**: warmup rollout 437.1 s vs 434.9/436.5 s for FA3 baselines. No gain; reverted.
+- **KV page size 64**: decode step 33 ms vs 27 ms. Killed mid-run, reverted.
+- **GPU/CPU optimizer split** (`--optimizer-offload-fraction 0.5`): steady-state CPU Adam is only ~9 s
+  (the 44 s first step is one-off state allocation, hidden in the untimed warmup). Timed optimizer 9.0 -> 4.8 s
+  but fwd/bwd got ~9 s slower with optimizer states resident on GPU. Net neutral-negative; reverted.
+- **TP comm overlap** (`--tp-comm-overlap`): TransformerEngine user-buffer assertion with dynamic
+  (variable-token) micro-batches. Reverted.
+- **Less recompute than selective-with-mla_up_proj** (only `moe_act`): CUDA OOM (120.9 GiB allocated) -
+  stored MLA up-projection activations for 32k-token micro-batches are far larger than estimated. Reverted.
+## Files changed
+- `/app/launch/run_step.py`: `--skip-actor-forward-only`; selective recompute (above).
+- `/root/miles`: `miles/ray/specs/train.py`, `miles/backends/training_utils/loss/hub/losses.py`,
+  `miles/backends/megatron_utils/actor.py`, `miles/utils/arguments.py`,
+  `miles/backends/megatron_utils/model.py` (timing logs only).
+- `/sgl-workspace/sglang/python`: two new Triton MoE config JSONs listed above. No code changes.
